newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude off on earnings, merger doubts.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude off on earnings, merger doubts.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc shares fell Wednesday on Wall Street fears that the medical devices maker may not meet fourth-quarter earnings expectations.
The shares were off 1-3/4 to 37-1/8.
"It's my sense that the fourth quarter, while operationally not bad, wasn't a gangbusters quarter," said Dain Bosworth medical technology analyst Rachael Scherer.
The First Call consensus estimate for St. Jude's fourth quarter earnings is $0.49 per share, up from $0.44 a year ago.
"The results will probably come in two cents short of $0.49," said UBS Securities analyst Samuel Navarro.
Analysts said there were also concerns about St. Jude's proposed acquisition of Ventritex Inc.
They also said investors' perception of St. Jude may become confused in the coming year by the company's involvement in several complex acquisitions.
"There are some investors who are saying they may just come back at a later date, when things are a little more certain," Scherer said.
A spokesman for St. Paul, Minn.-based St. Jude said it had no news to report on any of the issues raised by analysts.
"We have released no news. We have maintained that three of the four transactions we announced in October are closed," said spokesman Peter Gove.
He said the company continues to expect the Ventritex deal to close by the end of the current quarter.
St. Jude's purchases of Telectronics Pacing Systems Inc and Medtel, both affiliated with Pacific Dunlop Ltd, have been completed, Gove said.
Also settled are Ventritex's disputes with the Intermedics unit of Sulzer AG's Sulzer Medica, Gove said.
The closings of these deals, which made the Ventritex purchase feasible, are going to make St. Jude's fourth-quarter and first-quarter results confusing, analysts said.
The size and number of related write-offs and other special items have not been determined and remain questions weighing on the minds of investors, analysts said.
St. Jude, the world's largest maker of heart valves, is scheduled to release fourth-quarter results on February 5.

In addition to concerns about earnings and the mergers, J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Weinstein said Ventritex is encountering delays ramping up production of its new Contour implantable defibrillator, causing further worries about St. Jude's future challenges as Ventritex's parent.

St. Jude, also a leader in pacemaker production, said in October that it would take several bold steps to diversify into the growing market for implantable defibrillators, of which California-based Ventritex is a mid-sized manufacturer.
St Jude's interlocking deals with Ventritex and the three other companies were greeted as a masterful victory for Chief Executive Ron Matricaria, but they were also seen as risky.
The Ventritex purchase still must be approved by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, the U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission, and shareholders.
"The closing of the Ventritex deal is probably a few weeks late...We're looking at early March, maybe late February," Navarro said.
The longer the deal drags into 1997, "the further into 1998 you have to look for good comparisons...If you're an investor, it's a question of how long you want to wait," Scherer said.
